title: Relation Extraction using Large Language Models: A Survey (ACL 2020-2023)
Relation Extraction using Large Language Models: A Survey

note: Comprehensive survey of 137 RE papers from ACL 2020-2023

label: DREEAM
description: Self-trained RoBERTa using automatically generated evidence. Most accurate system for DocumentRE as of 2023.

label: UNIRE
description: Joint entity-relation model using 2D table representation. SOTA on ACE04/ACE05.

label: FSRE
description: Hybrid prototypical networks with contrastive learning. SOTA on FewRel 1.0/2.0.

label: S2ynRE
description: GPT-2/GPT-3.5 generating synthetic RE data with two-stage self-training. Surpasses SOTA on few-shot RE.

label: MCMN
description: Multi-Choice Matching Networks with triplet-paraphrase pretraining. Unifies zero/few-shot RE tasks.

label: ZS-BERT
description: Sentence-BERT for zero-shot relation classification via contextual representation learning.

label: CORE
description: Counterfactual Analysis Relation Extraction addressing entity bias through causal graphs.

label: mREBEL
description: mBART-50 pre-trained seq2seq model for multilingual triplet extraction.

label: TACRED
description: Large-scale sentence-level RE dataset for slot filling. 41 person/organization relations. Revised as TACREV and RE-TACRED.

label: FewRel
description: Few-shot RE benchmark. 100 relations. Standard train/val/test splits for few-shot evaluation.

label: ACE 2005
description: Multi-lingual IE benchmark from 2005 Automatic Content Extraction evaluation. Used for joint entity and RE.

label: SemEval-2010 Task 8
description: Multi-way semantic relation classification benchmark.

label: RoBERTa
description: Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining. Dominant backbone for supervised RE.

label: T5
description: Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer. Excels in few-shot and zero-shot RE via seq2seq formulation.

label: PubmedBERT
description: Domain-specific BERT pre-trained on PubMed. Most robust for biomedical RE.

label: CLIP
description: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training. Used for multimodal RE visual features.

label: Prototypical Networks
description: Meta-learning approach creating class prototypes from support set examples. Foundation for few-shot RE methods like FSRE.

label: Contrastive Learning
description: Learning representations by contrasting positive and negative pairs. Widely used in few-shot RE (FSRE, PEMSCL, CFRL).

label: NLI-based RE
description: Converting RE task to Natural Language Inference formulation. Effective for biomedical low-resource settings.

label: Synthetic Data Generation for RE
description: Using GPT models to generate synthetic training data for RE. S2ynRE approach surpasses SOTA on few-shot.

title: BERT-based Model Dominance in Supervised RE
description: BERT and variants (RoBERTa, SciBERT, PubmedBERT) consistently achieve SOTA in standard supervised RE settings. LLMs (GPT, T5) excel only in few-shot/zero-shot scenarios or synthetic data generation.
implications_for_few_shot: For our Enox extraction pipeline without fine-tuning, we are in the 'few-shot/zero-shot' regime where LLMs DO excel. But we need structured prompts (like ChatIE/RHF) to unlock this potential.

title: Joint Models Outperform Pipelines (for Supervised)
description: In supervised settings, 'best-performing joint approach consistently outperforms best pipeline model.' But this is for fine-tuned models. For LLM-based extraction, pipeline decomposition (ChatIE, RHF) is better.
implications_for_few_shot: Our pipeline approach (extract entities, then relations) is correct for LLM-based extraction. The 'joint is better' finding applies to fine-tuned supervised models, not our use case.

title: Evidence Selection Critical for Document-Level RE
description: Top document-level RE methods (DREEAM, SIEF, E2GRE) all incorporate evidence selection — identifying which sentences contain relevant information before extraction. This is an attention mechanism.
implications_for_few_shot: Our extraction prompts should tell the model which parts of the abstract to focus on. For full papers, a pre-filtering step identifying evidence sentences would dramatically help.

title: GPT-Generated Synthetic Data Surpasses SOTA
description: S2ynRE uses GPT-2/GPT-3.5 to generate synthetic RE training data with two-stage self-training, surpassing SOTA on few-shot RE. Chinchilla-like insight: more synthetic data > less real data.
implications_for_few_shot: We could use our deep extractions as seeds to generate MORE synthetic few-shot examples via GPT, amplifying our few-shot effectiveness.

title: Relation Descriptions Are Critical Across All Methods
description: Multiple papers confirm that clear relation type descriptions improve RE performance: AutoRE +44%, ZS-BERT uses relation descriptions for zero-shot, MCMN uses paraphrased relations. This is consistent across supervised, few-shot, and zero-shot settings.
implications_for_few_shot: Our Enox relation schema definitions MUST include clear descriptions with examples. This is the highest-leverage intervention available.
